BACKFILLED from bench20/RUNLOG.md Phase B and the three correlations CSVs. status=partial because no feature reaches p<0.05 by Spearman and none would survive multiple-testing correction across 11 features; the analysis ran to completion but does not support a model. Interface H-bond count is the only feature passing |rho|>=0.3 in all three subsets, and its sign is negative, meaning more H-bonds associates with lower log10 Kd, i.e. tighter binding. dG_norm strengthens as wrong models are removed (0.205 to 0.359), which is consistent with structural error diluting a real signal but is equally consistent with noise at n=16. Relaxed-model PRODIGY (rho 0.162, n=20) is no better than the crystal baseline (0.0925) in any meaningful sense at this sample size. - [2026-11-04T0300Z_interface-kd_structure-quality](runs/2026-11-04T0300Z_interface-kd_structure-quality/) — status **partial**, **backfilled** (not reproducible here), no `code_version` — producing code unidentified
BACKFILLED from bench20/RUNLOG.md Phase B. status=partial because 4 of 20 complexes are structurally wrong and were nonetheless retained for the correlation analysis (decision: keep all 20, report with and without). 1zvh, 3qhy and 5szj are explained by low ipTM (0.15-0.27). 5bnq is the concerning case: ipTM 0.85 but DockQ 0.03 with fnat 0 in all five models, confirmed by an independent alignment-based contact check, so it is not a chain-mapping artefact but a confidently wrong prediction. Relaxation slightly degrades agreement on average (-0.03) and badly for 4bkx. A PRODIGY baseline from an earlier superseded selection exists at archive/superseded_phaseA/prodigy_crystal_superseded_selection.csv and is a different selection, not a predecessor of this run. ::: ::: ## Validating the record `check_runs.py` at the repository root validates every manifest against the required fields, confirms each listed output exists, re-hashes every recorded input to detect results computed from a since-changed dataset, and checks supersession consistency. Run it before every render: ```bash python3 check_runs.py # errors exit 1 python3 check_runs.py --strict # warnings also exit 1 ``` Add a run with `new_run.py`, which captures tool versions, the git SHA and input hashes automatically. It refuses to copy large or binary artefacts into `runs/` — those are recorded by path and hash and left where they live — and refuses to re-run an existing track/stage/slug unless you say what it supersedes.
